notes: Not a section — a primitive that appears in several. Two of the four kinds are now CSS components, not drawings: the blast radius is a .blast box grid and the boundary chain is a .pipe spine. So the first thing this case tests is that a run reaches for the COMPONENT and does not draw an SVG out of habit — checks/diagram.sh will report `legend` and `box-json` as invented classes, but a run that hand-rolls a blast radius from .box and .edge passes every mechanical check while throwing away reflow and comparability. That needs a reader. The two surviving SVG kinds are the ER fragment and the lifecycle, and NO FIXTURE HERE EARNS EITHER: rails-only-small adds one nullable column, monorepo-contract has no state machine. Covering them needs a new fixture with a migration and a status enum; until then diagram.sh checks those two layouts against the template itself and nothing else does. What no script settles either way: whether the figure is TRUE, and whether it is legible. Run with --visual and look at the PNGs.

cases.expected_output: A .blast box grid in section 4, reaching from the new column through the model to the unchanged query that scopes the selectable list, with a .legend. NO SVG at all: no lifecycle, because archived_at is a timestamp and not a state machine, and no ER fragment for a single-column add.
expectations: The blast radius is a .blast box grid with a .legend, not an SVG — a run that draws it with .box and .edge has thrown away reflow and comparability while passing every mechanical check
Exactly the figures this diff earns: no lifecycle, because a nullable timestamp is not a state machine and drawing one would invent states the code does not have, and no ER fragment for one column
Solid border is changed, dashed is unchanged-and-affected, and the legend says which is which
The panel shows something the two lists cannot: the unchanged query sitting beside the changed column, as one frame rather than two sets

Where the finding is that something STOPS at a hop, the note under the panel says so in words — adjacency cannot express a directed edge, and this is the case where a run is most likely to reach for SVG instead
Read the PNGs from --visual if any SVG was drawn at all: nothing overlaps, no label leaves its box, and both themes are legible

cases.expected_output: A .pipe chain for archived_at inside the flow that owns it, with the nullable/non-null mismatch named at the hop it happens, plus the .blast grid for section 4. Still no SVG: no state machine, and one column does not earn an ER fragment.
expectations: A .pipe chain exists for archived_at and names the mismatch at the hop it occurs, rather than leaving the reader to compare two boxes
The chain is a .pipe, not an SVG boundary chain — the terminal node is filled, so the thing the chain arrives at is last

The budget is respected: one figure per section, and a second only where the mechanism is genuinely different — a chain inside a flow and a blast grid in section 4 qualify, two views of one call path do not
No ER fragment: one column plus its immediate neighbours does not earn one, and if the missing time_entries association is mentioned it is mentioned as ABSENT, which is the only reason to raise it
The dashed boxes in section 4 are exactly the unchanged consumers, selectableProjects and ProjectSelector, and nothing changed by the diff is dashed
Read the PNGs from --visual if any SVG was drawn: nothing overlaps, and both themes work
